children: NIKE, Inc. Class B (NYSE:NKE) faces pressure as Truist cuts NKE to Hold and trims its $42 target amid weak footwear demand and a 12‑year low premarket print, even as the company readies fiscal Q1 results, names Jane Ewing CCO, shifts production to Vietnam, and extends Brazil distribution.
Nike Cut To Hold; Targets Trimmed
: Truist cut Nike (NKE) to Hold and trimmed its target to $42, citing weak footwear demand and softer trends at Dick’s. Shares hit a 12-year low near $38.17 in premarket.
: NIKE (NKE) will report fiscal Q1 2027 results Oct 1, 2026 after market close and host a conference call at 2:00 p.m. PT; archived webcast available through Oct 29, 2026
: NIKE (NKE) names Jane Ewing Executive VP and Chief Commercial Officer, effective Sept. 7; announcement lists title and start date only, no pay, reporting lines, or duties disclosed.
: NIKE Class B (NKE) shifted production to Vietnam amid U.S.–China tariffs. The move boosted Vietnamese exports to the U.S. and reflects broader supply‑chain realignment away from China.
Grupo SBF Extends Nike Brazil Deal
: Nike Class B (NKE) distribution in Brazil extended with Grupo SBF through May 31, 2034, maintaining Grupo SBF as the local distributor and confirming the new contract end date.
